items.t: Sponsored the DUMP Red Tape Act, which the House passed, to let small business owners report unnecessary regulations so Congress can review them.
items.q: I’m very proud to see the House pass my bill, the DUMP Red Tape Act, to give small business owners a direct line to make their voices heard, report unnecessary regulations, and ensure those complaints are documented and reviewed so Congress can take action.

items.t: Introduced two bills that the House Committee on Small Business advanced with bipartisan support.
items.q: The House Committee on Small Business today advanced two bills introduced by Congressman Tony Wied (R-WI) with bipartisan support.

items.t: Said he wants to increase small business participation and opportunities to provide expertise to the federal government.
items.q: I look forward to working closely with them to ensure we increase their participation and provide them with opportunities to share their expertise with our federal government.

items.t: Secured $12.4 million for Community Funding Projects in Northeast Wisconsin with House passage of the final FY26 appropriations bills.
items.q: Rep. Tony Wied secured $12.4 million for Community Funding Projects in Northeast Wisconsin with yesterday’s passage of the final appropriations bills to fund the government for FY26.

items.t: Advocated for a $30 million Port Infrastructure Development Program grant for Wisconsin, which the U.S. Department of Transportation announced.
items.q: The U.S. Department of Transportation announced today that Wisconsin will receive a $30 million grant through its Port Infrastructure Development Program, following Congressman Wied’s advocacy for the funding.

items.t: Was appointed Chairman of the House Small Business Committee's Subcommittee on Contracting and Infrastructure.
items.q: The House Committee on Small Business announced that Congressman Tony Wied (R-WI) has been appointed Chairman of the Subcommittee on Contracting and Infrastructure.
